//: Wine grape. Agronomic entries are scoped by deviceNamePattern to placeholders (%vineyard%) — rename devices to match or replace the pattern with deviceProfiles before trusting an alert. Thresholds are the published extension figures cited in each entry; they are starting points, not calibrations.
//months: activeMonths are California coastal and interior timing: budbreak March–April, bloom May, veraison July–August, harvest August–October.
//enabled: Enabled: checks whose threshold is a published figure the sensor measures directly — air, leaf and soil temperature, humidity, durations, rates, pH. Disabled: checks whose threshold depends on this soil or this probe (volumetric moisture, EC, N, the 'wet' cut-off of a leaf-wetness sensor) or that need the forecast block — each says what to set before enabling it.

checks.//: ═══ FLEET HEALTH — every pack carries these, so the pack runs on its own. None needs crop tuning. ═══

═══ SPRING FREEZE by stage ═══ University of Maryland (Fiola): swollen bud −3.3 °C (26 °F), burst bud −2.2 °C (28 °F), one leaf −2.2 to −1.7 °C, two leaves −1.7 to 0 °C. Source: https://extension.umd.edu/resource/grapevine-frostfreeze-damage-i-background-and-prevention
−1.7 °C is the one-leaf figure; shoots with two leaves can be injured anywhere up to 0 °C, so lower-lying blocks may want threshold 0.

FROST TONIGHT. FAO Frost Protection (Snyder, UC Davis): start wind machines at about 0 °C, and in any case before the crop's critical temperature. Raised up to 14 h ahead so the decision is made the evening before. DISABLED: needs the top-level forecast block and a Weatherbit key (see README, Forecast).

POWDERY MILDEW — the UC Davis (Gubler-Thomas) risk index. UC IPM: the index starts at 60 after 3 consecutive days with ≥ 6 continuous hours at 21–29.4 °C (70–85 °F); each such day adds 20 (only 10 if the day also reaches ≥ 35 °C for 15 minutes), and a day with fewer subtracts 10 — heat on such a day adds no further decline, since UC IPM caps the daily decline at 10 and the daily rise at 20; bounded 0–100. 0–30 low, 40–50 moderate, 60–100 high pressure. Raised at 60 with the UC spray intervals (sulfur dust / micronized sulfur / DMI: 7/10/14 days) in the alert; lower threshold to 40 to hear about moderate pressure too. Heat is judged on the hourly maximum, which reads any reading at or above 35 °C in an hour as the 15 minutes. Source: UC IPM, grape powdery mildew risk assessment, https://ipm.ucanr.edu/DISEASE/DATABASE/grapepowderymildew.html

DOWNY MILDEW primary infection — the 10:10:24 rule used in Ontario and Australia: at least 10 mm of rain with temperature above 10 °C through a 24 h period. This check totals rain only (integrating rain.intensity, mm/h); in California's growing season the temperature half is nearly always met, and a cold-spell exception is visible in the same alert window. UC IPM gives no rule of this kind: optimum 20–25 °C, range 10–29 °C, infection can take under 90 minutes. Sources: OMAFRA, https://onfruit.ca/2024/08/07/the-lowdown-on-downy-mildew-in-grapes/ ; UC IPM, https://ipm.ucanr.edu/agriculture/grape/downy-mildew/

BOTRYTIS BUNCH ROT. UC IPM uses the Broome model, a wetness × temperature index fitted on 4–20 h of wetness with temperature clamped to 12–32 °C (optimum 15–20 °C when wet); index ≥ 0.5 is the spray trigger. The index is not computed here; this raises on 4 h of near-saturation inside the model's temperature range, the shortest wetness the model was fitted on, so it is deliberately sensitive. Source: UC IPM, https://ipm.ucanr.edu/DISEASE/DATABASE/grapebotrytis.html

HEATWAVE, by consecutive days of daily maximum air temperature — the form every source uses. Enabled: three or more days above 40 °C, the South Australian Bureau of Meteorology heatwave definition quoted by Wine Australia and AGWA (the other half of it is five or more days above 35 °C). Disabled: three consecutive days at or above 35 °C, the grapevine heatwave used in Wine Australia project UA 1502 ("photosynthesis becomes compromised beyond 37 °C") — enable it for cooler regions; in the Central Valley it would fire most of the summer. Air temperature is only a proxy: exposed dark berries run 12–15 °C above air, and berry-surface temperature, exposure, wind and vine water status decide sunburn. Sources: Wine Australia UA 1502, https://www.wineaustralia.com/research/strategy-4-improving-resource-management/climate-adaptability/ua-1502 ; Wine Australia, https://www.wineaustralia.com/growing-making/environment-and-climate/managing-vines-through-heatwaves ; Gambetta et al. 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7819898/

params.label: heat stress (3 days at 35 °C or above)

checks.//: ROOT-ZONE SALINITY — grape: Maas–Hoffman threshold ECe 1.5 dS/m, above which yield declines. DISABLED until converted to what the probe reads. Maas–Hoffman thresholds are saturated-paste ECe. A soil probe reports bulk EC (or pore EC), which is not ECe: FAO 29 gives soil-water EC ≈ 2 × ECe at field capacity, and bulk EC is lower than pore EC and moves with water content. Convert before enabling — take a saturated-paste lab sample beside the probe and scale this threshold by the probe/ECe ratio. Source: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29, ch. 2 and Annex 1 (Maas & Grattan 1999), https://www.fao.org/4/t0234e/t0234e02.htm , https://www.fao.org/4/y4263e/y4263e0e.htm

SOIL pH — grape (vinifera prefers 6.5–7.0): outside 5.5–7.0. pH moves over seasons, not hours, so this is info and needs a day sustained; it stays open until the field is limed or acidified. Source: eXtension, "Soil pH in vineyards", https://articles.extension.org/pages/65269/soil-ph-in-vineyards

WINKLER INDEX — season heat summation, base 50 °F (10 °C), April 1 to October 31, by the daily average. Region I ≤ 2500 °F-days, II 2501–3000, III 3001–3500, IV 3501–4000, V > 4000 (Amerine & Winkler, UC Davis). Each boundary passed is raised as info, which is how a vintage running hot or cool shows up against the block's usual region.
